summary.intent: Run the GSD manager to oversee milestone progress, then discuss Phase 42 (API unpin integrity) to lock down implementation decisions before planning begins.
summary.outcome: Phase 42 discuss completed: CONTEXT.md and DISCUSSION-LOG.md written and committed with all gray areas resolved — silent 2XX + audit log for no-row unpin, outbox pattern with per-CID advisory lock for dedup race, read-only drift report for historical orphans, and several secondary decisions locked.

repo: The unpin endpoint (`POST /ipfs/unpin`) is guarded only by JwtAuthGuard — it never reads req.user before calling Kubo pin/rm, making it a cross-tenant data-destruction vector for any account holder.
Kubo v0.40 runs with the `server` profile and swarm port 4001 exposed publicly, meaning all pinned CIDs are advertised to DHT crawlers. Blobs are encrypted but CIDs are publicly discoverable.
Kubo port 5001 (API) was locked to loopback in Phase 29 — the NestJS API endpoint is the only external unpin path.
Writable-share saves drop prunedCids without unpinning — no cross-user legitimate unpin path exists today.
All current unpin callers (web hook, FUSE) ignore unpin errors silently (.catch(logger.warn) / let _ =), so API status code changes are forward-looking contract decisions, not behavioral ones.
BYO-IPFS capability uses a provider.unpin injection pattern — the current server-side unpin flow bypasses it entirely for BYO users.
IPNS records are published to the public IPFS network, enabling CID discovery via IPNS resolution without DHT crawling.
The Phase 30 web observability pipeline receives unpin warnings — any status code change will land there as metric noise.

code.finding: Upload-compensation path fires a global Kubo pin/rm on a CID that content-addressed dedup may share with another user — no ownership check.

Kubo v0.40 configured with `server` profile and swarm port 4001 exposed tcp+udp. Server profile disables local-network discovery only — public DHT participation and provider record broadcasting remain active.
Web unpin caller swallows all errors with .catch(logger.warn) — no client reads the HTTP status code, so 403 vs 2XX is a pure API-contract choice.
Shared-write save path drops prunedCids without calling unpin — no cross-user unpin happens through the share system.

workflow: The GSD discuss phase workflow uses a checkpoint JSON file to persist decisions incrementally, allowing partial session recovery.
Presenting analysis as menus before directly answering the user's question caused friction — direct answers with evidence should precede option lists.

Silent 2XX vs loud 403 for idempotent delete endpoints: 403 is an existence oracle risk if not uniform, and conflates benign races with attacks in monitoring; 2XX + audit log separates telemetry from response semantics.
Postgres advisory xact lock on hash(cid) is the standard recommendation for per-CID concurrency control around refcount-based decisions.

friction: Assistant initially re-presented option menus instead of directly answering the user's three specific questions about CID discoverability and endpoint exposure — required explicit user correction.
User hit a session limit mid-discussion and had to re-send their last message to continue.
The DHT exposure finding (staging compose Kubo config) required multiple bash probes before the hedge on public routing was resolved.
open_items: Wire provider.unpin into BYO-IPFS delete flows — deferred out of Phase 42 scope.
Read-only drift report job (pins in Kubo not in pinned_cids ∪ pending_unpins) to detect historical orphans — deferred as a monitoring/hygiene task, not part of the unpin integrity fix.
Phase 42 planning has not started — CONTEXT.md is ready but plan/execute steps remain.
Concurrent dedup-unpin race closure via advisory lock needs to be explicitly tasked in the plan — it was identified during discuss but not yet in a plan file.
